rationale: Published cohorts consistently demonstrate that recurrent de novo missense variants (notably p.Arg578Cys and p.Arg1146Cys) associate with a severe syndromic presentation characterized by intellectual disability, spastic diplegia/quadriplegia, and structural brain defects such as corpus callosum hypoplasia, cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, and perisylvian polymicrogyria. Additionally, biallelic variants can manifest as severe lower motor neuron disease mimicking lethal spinal muscular atrophy. However, the hypothesis that truncating or specific distal variants cleanly demarcate isolated spastic paraplegia or mild phenotypes without cognitive impairment is contradicted by recent reports: inherited truncating/splice-site variants (e.g., p.Gly877Valfs*36) exhibit marked variable expressivity within single pedigrees, extending to severe intellectual disability, global developmental delay, and autism, demonstrating that genotype-phenotype correlations are non-dichotomous and complex.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 13 unrelated individuals with de novo MAPK8IP3 variants (6 missense, 3 truncating), brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants, providing early evidence of genotype-phenotype correlations.

evidence.text: A heterozygous truncating canonical splice-site variant (c.2630-2_2630-1del, p.Gly877Valfs*36) co-segregated in a three-generation family across three affected individuals, who exhibited broad phenotypic discordance ranging from mild learning difficulties to global developmental delay with severe intellectual disability and autism, demonstrating that truncating variants are not restricted to isolated spasticity or mild non-syndromic presentations.

source.title: Characterization of a novel inherited splice-site variant in MAPK8IP3 expands the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders
source.quote: Notably, despite carrying an identical genotype, the three affected individuals exhibited marked interindividual variability in clinical severity, ranging from mild specific learning difficulties to global developmental delay with severe intellectual disability and autism.

conflicts: Truncating and splice-site variants do not consistently result in isolated motor phenotypes or milder non-cerebral disease; familial truncating variants produce marked variable expressivity including severe global developmental delay, severe intellectual disability, and autism in the same kindred.

Biallelic loss-of-function/compound heterozygous variants can produce lethal lower motor neuron disease (SMA-like), whereas heterozygous truncating alleles can present as variable dominant neurodevelopmental disorders rather than simple hereditary spastic paraplegia.

new_directions.question_text: Do dominant-negative mechanisms versus haploinsufficiency account for the differences in structural brain anomalies observed between recurrent missense variants in JNK/kinesin interaction domains and loss-of-function truncating variants?
new_directions.rationale: Recurrent missense variants cluster at critical adaptor domains and show consistent cortical and callosal malformations, whereas truncating variants display high clinical variability that may reflect variable nonsense-mediated decay or incomplete penetrance.

new_directions.question_text: What modifier genes or epigenetic factors drive the intrafamilial phenotypic divergence between mild learning difficulties and severe syndromic ID in familial truncating MAPK8IP3 pedigrees?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving modifiers in identically mutated familial cases will allow clinicians to predict prognosis and discern pure spasticity/motor involvement from severe cognitive impairment.
